description: Branch prediction hint __builtin_expect through LOOMORA_LIKELY / LOOMORA_UNLIKELY (used in core/src/c_api.cpp); the fallback is the plain condition, with identical behaviour.
reason: Compilers without __builtin_expect (MSVC, unknown compilers) take the fallback. platform_ids stays empty until the platform records exist (T059, T087) and the per-platform compiler is known (T115).

description: [[nodiscard]] on the internal C++ functions is_eol, eol_warning, abi_version and build_compiler through LOOMORA_NODISCARD; the fallback is an empty attribute, so the discarded-result warning is lost but behaviour is identical.
min_compiler: C++17 mode (__cplusplus >= 201703L or _MSVC_LANG >= 201703L): gcc 7, clang 3.9, msvc 19.11 (VS 2017 15.3)
reason: The backend is built as strict C++11 on every Legacy target (and as C++14 where MSVC or the CMake clang/MSVC STL combination imposes it), so those builds take the fallback; only a build in C++17 mode or later uses [[nodiscard]]. platform_ids stays empty until the platform records exist (T059, T087, T115).

description: Dark theme of the Windows Legacy UI (ui/legacy/windows-win32/dynfeatures.cpp): when the user's "apps use light theme" setting (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize\AppsUseLightTheme, read through advapi32 loaded at run time) is 0 and no high contrast scheme is on, the window and its controls use dark colours (text 14:1 on the background) and, through dwmapi!DwmSetWindowAttribute when it exists, a dark title bar. The fallback is the colours of the system, which every Windows version applies by itself.
min_compiler: not a compiler feature: looked up at run time, any compiler; needs the AppsUseLightTheme setting (Windows 10, build 1607 or 1703 to verify, and Windows 11); a dark title bar needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later
reason: Windows 2000 to 8.1 have no dark theme setting for applications: the value is missing, the feature is skipped and "dark-mode" is added to disabled_features of the probe record; the greeting stays legible with the system colours. Exercised on Windows 11 only (light and dark). platform_ids stays empty until the Windows platform records exist (T088): the deliverable ids windows-x86 and windows-x64 are not platform records.

description: DPI awareness of the Windows Legacy UI: SetProcessDPIAware (user32) is looked up at run time and called before the window exists, the layout and the GUI font are then scaled to the system DPI. The fallback is not to call it.
min_compiler: not a compiler feature: looked up at run time, any compiler; SetProcessDPIAware exists since Windows Vista
reason: Windows 2000 and XP do not export SetProcessDPIAware: the call is skipped and "dpi-awareness" is added to disabled_features. Nothing is lost there, those systems do not virtualize the DPI, so the program already sees the real one (the layout is still scaled by it). Only the system level is requested: a window moved to a monitor of another DPI is stretched by the system. Exercised on Windows 11 at 100% only. platform_ids stays empty until the Windows platform records exist (T088).

description: High contrast query of the Windows Legacy UI: SystemParametersInfoW(SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST), looked up at run time in user32; when a high contrast scheme is on, the dark theme of the UI is not applied and the system colours stay. The fallback is to assume no high contrast scheme.
min_compiler: not a compiler feature: looked up at run time, any compiler; SPI_GETHIGHCONTRAST is available since Windows 2000
reason: Every Windows of the range (2000 to 11) is believed to export SystemParametersInfoW with this action, so the skip is a defensive path that is not expected to be taken; it is declared because the code can take it. The controls use system colours by default, so a high contrast scheme is respected even without the query. Not exercised with a high contrast scheme on. platform_ids stays empty until the Windows platform records exist (T088).

description: Peak memory of the Windows Legacy UI in probe mode: GetProcessMemoryInfo (PeakWorkingSetSize) from psapi.dll, loaded from the system directory at run time. The fallback is peak_rss_kb = -1 in loomora_probe_record, which the record shows as null.
min_compiler: not a compiler feature: looked up at run time, any compiler; psapi.dll is part of Windows 2000 and later
reason: The measure is best effort (ui-contract.md): when psapi.dll or the function is absent the probe record has a null peak_rss_kb and "peak-memory" in disabled_features. Not expected on Windows 2000 SP4 and later (psapi.dll ships with it, to verify on a real system); the skip path was not exercised. platform_ids stays empty until the Windows platform records exist (T088).

description: Alignment of the text of the wrapped end-of-life warning label of the Linux Modern UI (ui/modern/linux-gtk3/main.c, set_label_text_start): gtk_label_set_xalign(label, 0) when the GTK headers are 3.16 or later (every GTK 4 header too). The fallback is gtk_misc_set_alignment(label, 0, 0.5) of the 3.10 API (GtkMisc, deprecated in 3.14 and removed in GTK 4); the text is left-aligned the same way in both, mirrored in a right-to-left locale.
min_compiler: gtk 3.16 headers: GTK_CHECK_VERSION(3, 16, 0) and GDK_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED >= GDK_VERSION_3_16 (ui/modern/linux-gtk3/gtk_compat.h); always on with GTK 4 headers. Not a compiler feature.
reason: Headers older than GTK 3.16 (a distribution of 2014 or 2015 such as Ubuntu 14.04, GTK 3.10) and the floor build (-Dgtk_floor=true, GDK_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED pinned to 3.10) take the GtkMisc fallback. No platform of validation/platforms/ takes it: linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 has GTK 3.24.41 headers and takes the modern path. The fallback path was compiled and run only through the floor build on that platform (GTK 3.24 runtime, not a real GTK 3.10); a real GTK 3.10 system was not tried.

description: Scrollbar of the greeting of the Linux Modern UI (ui/modern/linux-gtk3/main.c, create_scroller): gtk_scrolled_window_set_overlay_scrolling(scroller, FALSE) when the GTK headers are 3.16 or later (every GTK 4 header too), so that the scrollbar stays visible beside the text of a long greeting. The fallback is not to call it: GTK 3.10 has no overlay scrollbars, its scrollbar is always visible and takes room, which is what the call restores on newer GTK (the default there is an overlay hidden until the pointer moves).
min_compiler: gtk 3.16 headers: GTK_CHECK_VERSION(3, 16, 0) and GDK_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED >= GDK_VERSION_3_16 (ui/modern/linux-gtk3/gtk_compat.h); always on with GTK 4 headers. Not a compiler feature.
reason: Headers older than GTK 3.16 and the floor build take the fallback; the greeting then has the scrollbar of the toolkit in use (always visible on a real 3.10, an overlay hidden until hover on a 3.16+ runtime). No platform of validation/platforms/ takes it: linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 builds with GTK 3.24.41 headers and takes the modern path. Visible difference measured with screenshots in WSLg: the floor build shows no scrollbar on a 1,000-character greeting, the default build shows one.

description: GTK 4 branch of the Linux Modern UI (ui/modern/linux-gtk3/main.c, gtk_compat.h, gtk_compat.c), selected at build time by the meson option -Dgtk_api=4 (dependency gtk4 instead of gtk+-3.0) and in the code by GTK_MAJOR_VERSION >= 4 (LOOMORA_GTK4): the same window content with the GTK 4 API (gtk_window_set_child, gtk_box_append, margins, GtkEditable text, a GMainLoop, the first display taken from the after-paint signal of the frame clock). The fallback is the GTK 3 UI, which is the default build. Differences of the GTK 4 branch: the end-of-life warning is a plain box (warning icon, text, close button) because GtkInfoBar is deprecated since 4.10 and has no replacement, so it has no warning background; the display time of the probe is the end of the first painted frame instead of the first draw.
min_compiler: gtk 4.0 headers (GTK_MAJOR_VERSION >= 4), built with -Dgtk_api=4; tried with GTK 4.14.5 and GCC 13.3. Not a compiler feature.
reason: GTK 4 is opt-in (-Dgtk_api=3 is the default), so every deliverable takes the GTK 3 path, linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 included even though its libgtk-4-dev is installed: the GTK 3 UI is the one of all the trials, the floor of the UI is GTK 3.10 and a system without GTK 4 stays served. On GTK 4.14.5 in WSLg the branch builds without a warning, passes the 15 reference vectors and the probe checks; the Mesa EGL warnings it prints on standard error under WSLg ("libEGL warning" lines, 134 bytes on the X11 backend, 265 on the default Wayland backend) come from the OpenGL renderer, not from the UI; on the Wayland backend they disappear with GSK_RENDERER=cairo or LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1. The GTK 4 build has no trial verdict.
